9e7d0ed0ee13c063e15d90d82e7a08442c7220f8.summary: NCSC malware analysis (TLP:CLEAR, Version 3, 7 November 2024) of Pygmy Goat, a 32-bit Linux shared object reported on Sophos XG firewalls. It is loaded into sshd via LD_PRELOAD and gives backdoor access. It is woken by an ICMP port knock or a magic SSH banner, then connects to a TLS-protected C2 channel. Commands cover a remote shell, packet capture, cron tasks and a reverse SOCKS5 proxy built on EarthWorm. The report says the embedded root certificate names FortiGate, which suggests FortiGate may have been an intended target. It states the techniques are not novel. No threat actor is named.

Example data in the report was generated in a virtual environment, not taken from any victim or actor.
The report says design choices suggest it may have been intended for FortiGate devices, and also that it could target a range of Linux devices.
The embedded root certificate claims to have been issued by FortiGate, Fortinet Ltd.
EarthWorm is described as not directly malicious, though threat actors have used it according to other reporting.
A footnote says the 2009 OpenSSH version string was presumably chosen because developers thought it unlikely to appear naturally.
